statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum possible bitwise XOR of all elements after applying the operation any number of times. Equivalently, let b range over all arrays of length len(nums) such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), b[i] is a bitwise submask of nums[i] (i.e., every 1-bit of b[i] is also a 1-bit of nums[i], or (b[i] AND nums[i]) = b[i]); then r = max { b[0] XOR b[1] XOR ... XOR b[len(nums)-1] }. Equivalently, r = nums[0] OR nums[1] OR ... OR nums[len(nums)-1], the bitwise OR of all elements of nums.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= 134217727 (i.e., r < 2^27).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), r >= nums[i] (ordinary integer ordering).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] is a bitwise submask of r; equivalently, (nums[i] AND r) = nums[i], or (nums[i] OR r) = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every non-negative 64-bit integer y, if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) we have (nums[i] AND y) = nums[i] (i.e., every nums[i] is a submask of y), then r <= y.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every array b of length len(nums) such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), b[i] is a bitwise submask of nums[i] (i.e., (b[i] AND nums[i]) = b[i]), the bitwise XOR b[0] XOR b[1] XOR ... XOR b[len(nums)-1] is at most r (ordinary integer ordering).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an array b of length len(nums) such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), b[i] is a bitwise submask of nums[i] (i.e., (b[i] AND nums[i]) = b[i]), and b[0] XOR b[1] XOR ... XOR b[len(nums)-1] = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Under these conditions, the result returned by maximum_xor for nums equals the result returned by maximum_xor for nums'.
preconditions: For two arrays nums and nums' of length n = len(nums), both satisfy 1 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000 and 0 <= nums'[i] <= 100000000; and there is a permutation π of {0,...,n-1} such that nums'[i] = nums[π(i)] for every i.

statement: For every r and r', if maximum_xor nums returns r and maximum_xor nums' returns r', then r <= r' (ordinary integer ordering).
preconditions: For two arrays nums and nums' of the same length n with 1 <= n <= 100000, both satisfying for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000 and 0 <= nums'[i] <= 100000000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums[i] is a bitwise submask of nums'[i] (i.e., (nums[i] AND nums'[i]) = nums[i]).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every bit position k with 0 <= k < 64, if every element nums[i] has bit k equal to 0, then r has bit k equal to 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.
